question: Will Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant be connected to offsite grid power on October 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo as of ~Oct 2-3 2026: ZNPP connected via the single 330 kV Ferosplavna-1 line (restored Sep 7 after an Aug 20 to Sep 7 total loss). Base rate: over Jun to early Oct 2026, about 15% of days were in complete loss of offsite power (dominated by one 18-day outage); most of the ~10 losses since June lasted hours and same-day restorations count as YES. The 11-day horizon from a connected state gives a hazard of a long outage still running on Oct 17 of roughly 8-15%. Fragility is elevated: a single line, ZTPP transformers damaged by drones Sep 19/20/27, ceasefire for repairs not yet secured. No human market found (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers: none on this contract).
calls.dossier:
- Status quo as of ~Oct 2-3 2026: ZNPP on a single offsite line, 330 kV Ferosplavna-1. The 750 kV Dniprovska line has been out repeatedly (out since 24 Mar 2026 per IAEA; the question background says disconnected again 23 Sep 2026). Sources: IAEA updates via search snippets; question background citing Update 369 (~2 Oct).
- 20 Aug 2026: 26th complete loss of offsite power (LOOP) of the war. Plant ran on diesel until Ferosplavna-1 was reconnected on the evening of 7 Sep 2026 under an IAEA-brokered local ceasefire (NEA status page; Al Jazeera 29 Aug 2026: diesel stock about 10 days, off-site diesel storage reportedly empty).
- 4 Aug 2026: LOOP lasting about 1 hour (12th of 2026, 24th of the war; Ukrainska Pravda 4 Aug). 8 Aug: brief LOOP. Three LOOPs in the first 8 days of August. 13 of 25 LOOPs fell in the 4 months to August.
- A Ukrainian article headline (NV) mentions a '15th blackout since start of 2026'; date unverified (page blocked).
- Drone strikes on 19, 20 and 27 Sep 2026 damaged Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant transformers that are vital for ZNPP offsite power. The IAEA is negotiating an 8th localized repair ceasefire (Ukrinform, 112.ua, 3 Oct 2026). A radiation monitoring station was disabled on 22 Sep.
- Precedent: the 23 Sep to 23 Oct 2025 LOOP lasted 30 days, the longest of the war. The Aug-Sep 2026 LOOP lasted 18 days. Long LOOPs need negotiated ceasefires and take weeks to fix; short ones are often restored within hours.
- Base rate over Jun to early Oct 2026: about 18 of about 125 days were in complete LOOP (~15% of days). Across 2025-2026 overall, roughly 10% of days were in LOOP (two long outages plus many short ones).
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the IAEA update describing status on or around 17 Oct 2026 (credible other sources as fallback), not Energoatom alone. Brief same-day interruptions that are restored count as YES.
- Event window: the single day of 17 Oct 2026; as of 6 Oct, 11 days remain until it.
- Could not find: the text of IAEA Updates 369/370 (fetch blocked), any LOOP reported for Oct 1-6 2026, or ceasefire status for the ZTPP transformer repairs.
- Markets: none found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.

calls.reasoning: Status quo (IAEA Update 369, ~2 Oct 2026): ZNPP is connected to the grid through the single 330-kV Ferosplavna-1 line. Dniprovska has been out since 23 Sep. Reference class: since June 2026, about 15% of days were spent in complete loss of offsite power, mostly from one 18-day outage. Most of the ~10 losses lasted hours, and a same-day restoration counts as YES. Starting from a connected state with 11 days to go, the NO path is a loss that needs a ceasefire to repair and is still running on 17 Oct. Past repairs of that kind took 2.5-4 weeks, so a loss would have to start soon and be severe. The risk is higher than usual: there is no redundancy, drones damaged the Zaporizhzhia thermal plant's transformers on 19, 20 and 27 Sep, and no repair ceasefire has been secured. calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the status quo (connected via one line as of ~2 Oct), the base rate (10-15% of days off-grid) and the 11-day horizon, so their spread of 0.82-0.86 is judgment. The one factual item reported by only one run is the drone damage on 19/20/27 Sep to the Zaporizhzhia thermal plant transformers that the offsite supply depends on, with the IAEA negotiating an 8th ceasefire. I cannot verify it without web access, but it fits the background statement that supply 'remains unstable', so I treat it as plausible. It nudges risk somewhat above the plain base rate. Because the plant is currently connected and a NO needs a long outage to be under way on the single date, I land at 0.84.
